note: One expectation index per contract directory. Each case names the structural violations that prove its point as (pointer, keyword) pairs; a validator's free-text message is deliberately never recorded, so a validator upgrade that rewords a message cannot turn these expectations red. The expected set must be a subset of what the validator reports, because a conditional rule often reports a broader violation alongside the specific one.

schema-version-foreign.proves: A document claiming a version this contract does not pin is rejected by const, which is what lets a producer map it to SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.

schema-version-missing.proves: Every contract document states the version it claims; omitting it is a root required violation, never a silent default to the current version.

detail-missing.proves: detail is required: a problem without an explanation is not a usable problem.

code-lowercase.proves: A problem code is upper snake case, so case is part of the identity and a lowercased code cannot be matched against a registered one by accident.

detail-multiline.proves: detail is single-line: a multi-line value is exactly the shape a copied traceback or exception message has, so the pattern refuses it.

detail-line-separator.proves: A guard written as [^\r\n] would accept U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR while a renderer still breaks the line on it; the contract rejects the separators too.

title-control-character.proves: A C0 control inside a title would survive into a log line or a header; the single-line rule covers every control character, not only CR and LF.

detail-leading-whitespace.proves: Templated text has no leading padding; padding is a sign the value was concatenated from somewhere else rather than rendered.

extra-traceback-property.proves: The root is closed, so a producer cannot bolt an internal diagnostic member onto a client-facing problem.

transport-binding-property.proves: The problem contract is transport-neutral; an HTTP status belongs to the adapter that maps this document onto a transport, not to the contract.

error-carries-a-message.proves: An error entry is (pointer, keyword) only. A free-text member is the exact channel through which validator text, and anything it quotes, would reach a client.

error-pointer-not-a-pointer.proves: A JSON pointer is empty or starts with '/'; a bare member name is not a pointer and would resolve nowhere in the client's document.

error-keyword-with-space.proves: keyword names a JSON Schema keyword, so it is a bounded structural token rather than a place to put a sentence.

errors-above-the-bound.proves: The error collection is finitely bounded, so one pathological document cannot turn a single problem into an unbounded response.
